Truck accidents on I-16 are particularly devastating. A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at highway speed can weigh 80,000 pounds, and the force of a collision between a commercial truck and a passenger vehicle at 65+ mph frequently produces traumatic brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, and fatalities. If a truck driver's fatigue, distraction, or impairment caused your crash on I-16, you may have claims against both the driver and the trucking company.

Abercorn Street: One of Savannah's Deadliest Roads

Abercorn Street is one of the deadliest roads in the City of Savannah: from 2020 through 2024, about 11 fatal crashes on Abercorn inside the city killed 12 people, tied with U.S. 17 for the most deaths of any city road (NHTSA FARS). Stretching from the Historic District south through Midtown and deep into the Southside suburbs, Abercorn carries enormous traffic volumes through a corridor lined with commercial development that generates constant turning movements, driveway conflicts, and parking lot access points.

DeRenne Avenue: Heavy Congestion Between I-516 and Truman Parkway

DeRenne Avenue is Savannah's primary east-west artery through the Midtown area, and it is notorious among local drivers for its dangerous conditions. According to the City of Savannah, the six-lane road is hindered by "heavy congestion and traffic queues" at peak hours, and that congestion creates a pressure-cooker environment where aggressive driving and crashes are common. The city's long-planned Project DeRenne won an $11.3 million federal grant for right-of-way in October 2026, but environmental approval is scheduled for 2027 and completion is targeted for 2034 (WTOC).

Georgia and South Carolina Laws for Accident Victims

Statute of limitations: Georgia gives accident victims two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33. South Carolina allows three years under S.C. Code § 15-3-530. Because I-95 crosses state lines, victims of crashes near the Georgia-South Carolina border need to be aware of both deadlines.

Comparative fault: Under O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, Georgia follows a modified comparative fault rule allowing recovery if you are less than 50% at fault, with your award reduced by your percentage of responsibility. South Carolina's threshold is slightly more favorable — recovery is allowed if you are less than 51% at fault.

Commercial vehicle regulations: Truck accidents on I-16, I-95, and I-516 may involve violations of federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration regulations governing driver hours of service, vehicle maintenance, cargo securement, and driver qualifications. These violations can serve as powerful evidence of negligence in your injury claim.

Wrongful death: When a highway crash kills a victim, Georgia's wrongful death statute (O.C.G.A. § 51-4-1) allows the surviving spouse, children, or parents to pursue compensation. South Carolina's wrongful death statute (S.C. Code § 15-51-10) provides similar rights.

When a government entity's failure to maintain a road causes a crash, injured victims may have a claim under Georgia's governmental immunity exceptions. Who owns the road sets the deadline: claims involving state routes such as I-16, I-95, I-516, and Abercorn require written notice to the state within 12 months (O.C.G.A. § 50-21-26), and the state is not liable for a road plan or design that substantially complied with the engineering standards in effect at the time (O.C.G.A. § 50-21-24(10)). Claims against the City of Savannah require written notice within six months (O.C.G.A. § 36-33-5), and counties cannot be sued unless a statute allows it (O.C.G.A. § 36-1-4), with claims due within 12 months (O.C.G.A. § 36-11-1).

Georgia Laws for Accident Victims

Statute of limitations: Georgia gives accident victims two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33.

Comparative fault: Under O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, Georgia follows a modified comparative fault rule allowing recovery if you are less than 50% at fault, with your award reduced by your percentage of responsibility.

Commercial vehicle regulations: Truck accidents on I-16, I-95, and I-516 may involve violations of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations governing driver hours of service, vehicle maintenance, cargo securement, and driver qualifications. These violations can serve as powerful evidence of negligence in your injury claim.

Wrongful death: When a highway crash kills a victim, Georgia's wrongful death statute (O.C.G.A. §§ 51-4-1, 51-4-2) allows the surviving spouse (or, if there is none, the children) to recover the full value of the decedent's life; if neither survives, the parents may recover under O.C.G.A. § 19-7-1.
